description: Laboratory experiments are based upon the corresponding theory course EEPC-208. An updated list of experiments is floated by the course coordinator before the beginning of each semester.
outcomes: Understand the time response of various control systems.
Describe the transfer function of different control systems.
Analyse the closed loop operation of different types of controllers.
Understand the frequency response of control operations.
experiments: Obtain the step response of first and second order systems and determine time-domain specifications from their transfer functions.
Determine the characteristics of LVDT and potentiometer error detectors for control applications.
Obtain the response of P, PI, PD, PID and relay control actions on one-time-constant and two-time-constant processes with and without delay.

Study a thermal system and its temperature control: obtain the transfer function from open-loop time response, determine the closed-loop response using PID and relay control actions, and compare the results.
Study the performance of a magnetic levitation system using P and PD control action and of DC motor position control.
Obtain the speed-torque characteristics of an AC servomotor and the speed control characteristics of a DC motor with a control parameter.
Design a lag or lead compensator for a given system, obtain its frequency response and analyze the result.
For a given transfer-function or state-space system, perform MATLAB simulations to obtain time-domain specifications, frequency-domain specifications and stability.
Study the performance of an industrial process for level control and flow control.
